answer: A stake-bonded reputation registry resists Sybil attacks by pricing identity itself: each agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove the agent submitted duplicate or fraudulent work. Like pigment mixed into a dye, the stake cannot be separated from the identity, so an attacker who spawns a thousand copies must fund every one. A harbor authority can add a small proof-of-work or verifiable credential check per identity, turning the dune of cheap fake agents into a real cost, while honest agents pay once and keep trading.
